newsitem.title: UK: Dated Brent eases, other North Sea crudes steady.
newsitem.headline: Dated Brent eases, other North Sea crudes steady.

text.p: Dated Brent crude eased on Tuesday but differentials for other regional crudes appeared to be holding despite a sustained margin squeeze which prompted Shell to reduce refinery throughput in Rotterdam, traders said.
A June 11-13 Brent cargo, kept from the paper chains by Phibro, was sold for July Brent +9 cents, eight cents weaker than the same buyer paid on Friday for a June 9-11 loader.
But most traders said the benchmark grade was still overvalued and supported by one aggressive buyer keen to keep published quotes strong this week to benefit a long Brent CFD position.
This week's CFDs slipped a couple of cents to talk at July Brent +3/+8 cents but still held a steep premium over next week (June 2-6) which was valued at July Brent -20/-16 cents.
Strong Brent and relatively weak refined product prices combined to squeeze refinery margins even further, with average cracking yields in Rotterdam dipping to $1.12 a barrel.
Shell on Monday became the latest refiner to scale back crude throughput, cutting by about 14 percent runs at its 350,000 barrels per day (bpd) Pernis plant.
The move followed similar cuts at the Texaco/BP Nerefco complex last week.
Depressed refining margins and lacklustre U.S. gasoline prices pushed cash Brent lower on Tuesday, July trading at $19.85 and $19.78 a barrel after a deal on Friday at $20.09.
But other North Sea grades like Statfjord and Ekofisk were holding their ground, traders said.

"It's very much a wait-and-see market at the moment and the market is certainly holding steady. (The margin squeeze) has had very little impact yet on the grades we're looking at," said a North Sea trader.
Russian Urals differentials were seen firming slightly on Tuesday having traded at a low of Dated Brent -$1.43 on Friday.
